title: Non-tight verifiable delay functions from a random oracle alone
formal: Historical question, resolved negatively: can a verifiable delay function with computational uniqueness be constructed in the parallel random oracle model alone when sequentiality is allowed to be substantially weaker than the honest evaluation time T, for example σ=T/2? The source’s tight impossibility theorem did not answer this question. The later general barrier shows that a perfectly complete candidate with polynomial query budgets either loses computational uniqueness or permits computation of its correct output in at most 6qᵥ online oracle rounds with constant success probability, after polynomial-query preprocessing. Here qᵥ is the verifier’s query bound. Thus even non-tight delay requirements exceeding this verification-scale depth cannot be obtained from the random oracle alone, whenever T is large enough relative to qᵥ.
context:
A proof of sequential work can have many valid outputs for one challenge. Such proofs exist in the random oracle model with non-tight sequentiality, so their existence did not answer the VDF question, which additionally requires a computationally unique output.

The 2020 paper ruled out perfect uniqueness and separately ruled out delay requirements very close to T. Computational uniqueness allows incorrect accepted outputs to exist as long as bounded-query adversaries cannot find them. The extracted passage asks about that remaining non-tight setting.

The CRYPTO 2025 result handles computational uniqueness with public-coin setup. The EUROCRYPT 2026 follow-up covers private-coin setup, even when its query budget grows polynomially with T. Its theorem therefore includes the source’s cheaper setup model.

The attacks may perform unrestricted local computation between bounded batches of oracle queries. Constructions using an additional repeated-squaring or other computational assumption are outside the pure oracle model and are not contradicted by this result.
why: Determines whether ideal hash access alone can support both publicly verifiable uniqueness and a substantial sequential delay, a central assumptions question for timed cryptography.
status_note: Read the original non-tight passage and ROM definitions, the current July 2026 major revision of the CRYPTO work, and the EUROCRYPT 2026 model and Corollary 1. Matched computational uniqueness, preprocessing and private-coin setup. The resolution is in the pure parallel query model; no ordinary polynomial-time attack or independent proof audit is claimed.

sentences: A verifiable delay function must take sequential effort to evaluate while its unique output can be publicly checked quickly.
The source asks whether a random oracle alone can provide this even with a weaker delay requirement such as half the honest time.
Proofs of sequential work do not settle the issue because they need not have unique outputs.
Published results in 2025 and 2026 rule out computationally unique VDFs, ultimately including private and expensive setup.
The historical question is resolved in the parallel oracle query model, where internal computation is unrestricted.

references.title: Can Verifiable Delay Functions Be Based on Random Oracles?
references.authors: Mahmoody, Mohammad; Smith, Caleb; Wu, David J.
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 3; PDF page 3

definitions: For security parameter λ, the shared oracle H maps finite binary strings to λ-bit strings, with independently uniform answers on new inputs and consistent answers on repetitions. A query round submits an arbitrary finite batch using only earlier answers; all answers in that batch arrive together. Total work counts oracle queries and sequential time counts rounds. Internal computation between queries is unrestricted in this model. A uniform scheme consists of Setupᴴ(λ,T), Evalᴴ(pp,x)=(y,π), and deterministic public Verifyᴴ(pp,x,y,π). Public parameters pp specify a finite uniformly samplable input set. For fixed H,pp,x the output y is fixed even if proof generation is randomized. Perfect completeness means every honestly generated output and proof is accepted. Setup, Eval and Verify have bounds qₛ,qₑ,qᵥ respectively; the source requires qₛ,qᵥ polynomial in λ and log T and qₑ≤T. The stronger 2026 model permits qₛ,qₑ polynomial in λ,T and evaluation in at most T rounds. Setup may hide its random coins; all verification information is public. Computational uniqueness forbids any adversary making polynomially many queries in λ,T from producing an accepted y′ different from the honest y, except with probability negligible in λ. Sequentiality at depth σ forbids a two-stage adversary, with the same polynomial total query budget, from outputting the honest y with non-negligible probability: the first stage sees pp and preprocesses, a fresh uniform x is then sampled, and the online stage receives x and has at most σ rounds. It need not output a proof. Negligible means smaller than λ^{−c} eventually for every fixed c>0. Probabilities include the oracle, setup, challenge and adversary coins. The later impossibility already holds with a random challenge in the uniqueness game; the 2020 source’s stronger adversarial-input and pointwise-oracle uniqueness cannot evade it. No algebraic or other hardness assumption is available in addition to H.
answer_criterion: Establish existence or impossibility in the source’s general, computationally unique non-tight regime. The published 2026 Corollary 1 supplies impossibility: for perfect completeness, one of its two attacks succeeds with probability at least 1/3. The sequentiality attack uses at most 6qᵥ online rounds and polynomially many total queries, including preprocessing; the other attack breaks uniqueness with polynomially many queries. This is a query-model separation, not a claim that every ordinary implementation has a polynomial-time attack.
